title: INDIAN AIR FORCE CONDUCTS EXERCISE SAHAYATA SETU AT AIR FORCE STATION JAMNAGAR
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence INDIAN AIR FORCE CONDUCTS EXERCISE SAHAYATA SETU AT AIR FORCE STATION JAMNAGAR Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 4:24PM by PIB Ahmedabad The Indian Defence Forces, under the guidance of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and Headquarters South Western Air Command (HQ SWAC), in coordination with participating national agencies and Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs), commenced the first day of Exercise Sahayata Setu, a multi-national Annual Joint Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Exercise (AJHE-26) at Air Force Station Jamnagar. The exercise is being conducted from 17-19 November 2026. The exercise commenced with a brainstorming seminar involving representatives from FFCs associated with the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), Bay of Bengal initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Co-operation (BIMSTEC) and Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (QUAD). Participating nations included Australia, Bangladesh, Comoros, Indonesia, Kenya, Madagascar, Malaysia, Maldives, Mauritius, Mozambique, Oman, Seychelles, Singapore, Somalia, South Africa, SriLanka, Tanzania, Thailand, United Arab Emirates, Yemen, Japan, United States of America, Myanmar and Nepal. Their participation highlighted the importance of multilateral cooperation, regional partnerships and collective preparedness in addressing humanitarian emergencies and complex disaster scenarios. The interactions also facilitated the exchange of experiences and best practices, strengthening international collaboration in Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Operations. Air Marshal PV Shivanand, Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, South Western Air Command delivered a keynote address and emphasised the need for integrated planning, joint capability development and seamless coordination among stakeholders to ensure a swift, effective and cohesive response to natural disasters and humanitarian emergencies. The exercise featured insightful deliberations by distinguished speakers from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Indian Army (IA), Indian Navy (IN), Indian Air Force (IAF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), relevant disaster management agencies and Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). The discussions focused on “India’s Growing Global HADR Footprint”, with case studies on Operation Amistad, Operation Brahma and Operation Sagar Bandhu, highlighting India’s expanding role in international humanitarian assistance, disaster relief and regional cooperation. Other key themes included “Leveraging Technology to Enchance Disaster Management and Joint Capability Enhancement for HADR Operations”. The deliberations examined the application of emerging technologies, enhanced situational awareness, coordinated operational planning and interoperability among participating agencies to strengthen preparedness and response capabilities in complex disaster scenarios. A QUAD working-level meeting towards synchronising effort towards HADR was also conducted during the afternoon session. Exercise Sahayata Setu further aims to familiarise participants with national and state level disaster management structures, delineate inter-agency responsibilities and validate established procedures for coordinated disaster response. The exercise will subsequently progress to scenario-based activities centred on a simulated severe cyclonic storm. These will involve reconnaissance, search and rescue, evacuation, relief operation and casualty management, followed by the activation of emergency operation centres, establishment of an incident command post, distribution of relief material and setting up of relief camps.
